newsitem.title: USA: Seagull completes South Hurghada well.
newsitem.headline: Seagull completes South Hurghada well.

text.p: Seagull Energy Corp said Tuesday said a delineation well has been completed at its 100 percent owned South Hurghada concession in Egypt.
The company also said it is proceeding to complete its application for a development lease covering the productive area at South Hurghada.

Trucking of oil production is expected to begin in the third quarter of 1997 at an estimated initial rate of 800 gross barrels per day, the company reiterated, adding it is expected to increase to about 4,000 barrels daily year-end.

Seagull said logs of the Wadi El Sahl 3 indicated three pay zones, two of which were tested. On the tests, oil flows were estimated at 500 barrels per day of 30-degree gravity oil from an upper Nukhul formation zone on artificial lift. A middle Nukhul zone tested 1,251 barrels daily of 30-degree API oil and a lower Nukhul zone was not tested.

The Wadi El Sahl 3 is in the vicinity of the Abu Marwa 1, completed earlier in 1997, and directly offsets two successful Wadi El Sahl exploratory wells drilled by the concession's former owner. Flow rates on tests at those two earlier exploratory wells measured 3,900 and 1,040 barrels daily.

The rig used to drill the Wadi El Sahl 3 well has been moved off that location to East Beni Suef, another concession, where it has started the first exploratory test to be drilled there. Seagull holds a 50 percent working interest and is the operator at East Beni Suef. Apache Corp holds the remaining interest. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
